Q1: Chromium exhibits several recognized significant hazards (Tier 1) including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and reproductive toxicity, environmental impact, inhalation toxicity, and organ/systemic effects. It also presents potential concerns for endocrine disruption and dermal/eye effects based on an expanded scientific perspective (Tier 2). Data regarding oral hazards are currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Chromium is listed as a potential endocrine disruptor by the TEDX list and is subject to the EPA's Drinking Water Standard, indicating significant health and regulatory concerns. No lists of low hazard were identified for this chemical.
Q3: Chromium is a very well-characterized element with a simple, well-defined structure and an exceptionally high number of scientific literature references (470,000). It possesses substantial toxicological data across various programs, though it has not undergone the most comprehensive IRIS or PPRTV assessments. Only one hazard class (oral) is categorized as data deficient.
